## What it does
Green fluorescent protein (GFP) from the jellyfish *Aequorea victoria* is an energy-transfer acceptor: it takes the blue chemiluminescence of the photoprotein aequorin and re-emits it as green fluorescent light [UniProt].

## The parts that matter
- The chromophore forms from residues 65–67, where a Ser-Gly cross-link creates a 5-imidazolinone ring [UniProt].
- Tyr66 is modified to (Z)-2,3-didehydrotyrosine, completing the light-emitting group [UniProt].
- InterPro classifies the whole chain as a GFP-like fluorescent protein [InterPro].
- The AlphaFold model is very confident, with a mean pLDDT of 96.6 [AlphaFold DB].

## What goes wrong when it breaks
The linked records contain no disease annotations for GFP. What the features do imply is that the cross-link at 65–67 is what makes the protein glow, so changes there would be expected to affect fluorescence [UniProt].
